metadata.indicator_name: Share of food expenditure in total expenditure for each income quintile, by area
metadata.data_features: Estimates are derived from Household Income and Expenditure Surveys (HIES) or Household Budget Surveys (HBS).
metadata.definition: Proportion of expenditure on food and non-alcoholic beverages in total household expenditure for each income quintile, by area.
metadata.calculation_methodology:
1. Calculation of the Indicator

It is calculated as the ratio between total expenditure on food and non-alcoholic beverages for each income quintile, by area (numerator), and total household expenditure for each income quintile, by area (denominator). The result is multiplied by 100.

P =
100 * gaqj
Gqj

Where:

  • gaiqj =Total household expenditure on food in quintile q and area j
  • Gqj = Total household expenditure in quintile q and geographic area j

      • 2. Calculation of income quintiles:

      Income quintiles are constructed by ranking households according to their per capita income, resulting in five equally sized groups. Quintile 1 comprises 20% of households with the lowest income, while quintile 5 includes 20% of households with the highest income.

      Household per capita income is defined as the ratio between total household income and the number of household members
metadata.comments:
Food expenditure refers to expenditure classified under Division 1 of the Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose (COICOP), developed by the Statistics Division of the United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs, “Food and non-alcoholic beverages”. This excludes expenditure on food consumed away from home, which is classified under Division 11, “Restaurants and accommodation services”.

For the estimation of expenditure, the concept of “household final consumption expenditure” is used. This includes both monetary and non-monetary expenditures incurred by households in the acquisition of goods and services to satisfy their needs. Within this framework, intermediate consumption expenditures—defined as those incurred in the production of other goods and services—as well as acquisitions of fixed assets, such as dwellings or other valuables, are excluded.
